findings.affected_requirement: Story 12.2 AC-2; FR-010 through FR-015; SC-002
findings.evidence: FR-031 says an unqualified CodeGraph failure or timeout must record a Warning and must not fail PreScan. That permits an index, status, identity, or completeness failure to fall back, contradicting FR-010 through FR-015 and docs/bmad/epics.md:1272-1277, which require CodeGraph readiness failure to stop PreScan. The downstream plan narrows the fallback to expansion alone at plan.md:132 and prepared-scan-contracts.md:54-56, but the accepted specification remains broader and therefore permits two incompatible implementations.
findings.correction_outcome: Revise FR-031 to state that only the bounded post-readiness related-file expansion operation may fall back. Explicitly require index, status, runtime, identity, path, completeness, and readiness failures to reject approval. Regenerate the plan set so every failure table and test seam uses that exact distinction.

findings.evidence: The Prepared Scan Manifest is defined as one per Repository at spec.md:160 and data-model.md:5, while FR-035 requires manifest ordinals to be contiguous 1..N. Research R-10 at research.md:81 and the planner contract at prepared-scan-contracts.md:12-14 instead assign one pair-global merged ordinal and retain those merged ordinals in each Repository manifest. Once entries interleave across Repositories, an individual manifest can contain ordinals such as 1,3,5 and cannot satisfy the per-manifest contiguous requirement.
findings.correction_outcome: Define the ordinal domains explicitly. Either store both a contiguous per-Repository manifest ordinal and a distinct contiguous pair-selection ordinal, or redefine the schema and terminology around a pair-level container while preserving one Repository per Scan. State which ordinal participates in each ID, fingerprint, uniqueness constraint, API projection, audit, replay comparison, and Story 12.3 handoff.

findings.affected_requirement: FR-022; FR-033 through FR-040; SC-001; SC-008
findings.evidence: The plan repeatedly promises deterministic GUIDs and SHA-256 fingerprints over length-prefixed UTF-8 scalars, but never defines the canonical byte grammar: schema/domain separator, exact field order, field tags, null encoding, integer and boolean encoding, GUID byte order, enum encoding, collection counts, nested child framing, or whether derived IDs are excluded. Data-model.md derives the manifest ID from the fingerprint while FR-035 can be read to include every identity-bearing scalar, leaving a possible circular ID/fingerprint definition. The existing authoritative seam demonstrates the required precision in ScanContextSnapshot.cs:74-105, which fixes field order, big-endian lengths, UTF-8, null encoding, digest truncation, UUID bits, and big-endian Guid construction.
findings.correction_outcome: Add a versioned canonical-envelope contract for manifest, classification, audit, File Code Unit, and deterministic GUID derivation. Enumerate included fields in exact order and define all scalar/list encodings, normalization, domain separators, derived-field exclusions, and UUID construction. Remove any ID/fingerprint cycle and add golden-vector plus independently reconstructed replay tests.

findings.evidence: The pair merge sorts by Repository identity but does not define how Guid Repository identities are canonically compared; Guid.CompareTo, canonical lowercase text, RFC byte order, and database ordering are not equivalent. The same requirement says every high-value seed must be retained, but neither the specification nor plan defines the high-value predicate or whether it means every qualifying candidate, every top-20 selected seed, or only selected seeds above the production fallback score. Research.md:81 and prepared-scan-contracts.md:11-14 repeat these undefined terms. Valid implementations can therefore choose different units and ordinals from identical inputs.
findings.correction_outcome: Define the Repository identity comparison representation and comparator, define high-value seed eligibility and its relationship to the 20-per-Repository seed bound, and specify cap behavior when qualifying candidates exceed bounds. Add tie, reversed-input, cross-Repository interleaving, and over-cap golden cases that prove the exact selected set and order.

summary: REVISE. The Windows-host runtime, exact CodeGraph/JDT-LS identities, no-CodeGraphContext boundary, safe XML design, additive compatibility, atomic pair transaction intent, planned-change trigger matrix, and Story 12.3 exclusion are otherwise well aligned and feasible against current source. Four High findings prevent ACCEPT: ambiguous CodeGraph fallback scope, contradictory per-manifest versus pair-global ordinals, an incomplete canonical identity/fingerprint byte contract, and undefined pair-selection comparators/high-value semantics. Read-only checks used Get-Content -Raw over every definition and authority artifact, rg -n searches over Story 12.2/12.3, PRD clauses, dated designs, Story 12.1 seams, and current production/tests, git status --short, and Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 over all 13 owned paths. No files, lifecycle state, index, branch, or Git history were changed.
